evidence: Singer John Holt introduced U-Roy to producer Duke Reid in 1970; Reid put him to work talking over existing Treasure Isle rocksteady rhythms, starting with Alton Ellis's 'Girl I've Got a Date' (1967), as documented in U-Roy's own biography accounts and Wikipedia's articles on 'Wake the Town' and U-Roy.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Play Ellis's original rocksteady vocal first, then U-Roy's version built on the same rhythm track three years later: the tune and the players are the same, but U-Roy talks, chants and ad-libs over the top instead of singing a fixed lyric, turning Reid's back catalogue into new records without a new song being written.

explanation.age13: Duke Reid, who owned Treasure Isle, gave U-Roy his first records to make in 1970 by having him talk over existing rocksteady rhythm tracks the label already owned, starting with a song by Alton Ellis. It made U-Roy a star and gave the label's old rhythms a second life.
explanation.adult: A label edge in the direct sense: Reid's catalogue of already-owned rhythm tracks was the raw material his own decision to pair with U-Roy turned into a new commercial format, toasting on record, that reused Treasure Isle's existing masters rather than paying for new backing tracks.
